lines.text: Tariffs are in the news a lot. So who actually pays them?
A tariff is a tax on goods brought in from another country.
It's paid by the company importing the goods, to its own government. In the U.S., to Customs.

scene.headline: The [importer] pays it
scene.sub: To U.S. Customs and Border Protection

lines.text: Say a store imports a hundred dollar item with a 25% tariff. The store owes twenty-five dollars at the border.
lines.say: Say a store imports a one hundred dollar item with a twenty-five percent tariff. The store owes twenty-five dollars at the border.

lines.text: The store can absorb that cost, or pass some of it on to shoppers through higher prices.
Studies of the 2018 and 2019 U.S. tariffs found most of the cost landed on American buyers, not foreign sellers.

scene.headline: 2018–19: most costs landed [at home]
scene.sub: Economic studies of the U.S. tariffs

lines.text: That's the money. See you at the next bell.
